worldcup.title: Post your questions for Terry Butcher
worldcup.summary: Is there anything you would like to ask the former Ipswich, Rangers and England defender? Terry Butcher has lived a full life in football. He won the Uefa Cup while playing for Ipswich under Bobby Robson; he was an England regular throughout the 1980s, winning 77 caps and playing at three World Cups; he captained Rangers in their late 1980s heyday; and he had a varied coaching career that started at Coventry City and took him to Australia, China and the Philippines. He’s also Pat Nevin’s cousin, one of only two England players born in Singapore, and, of course, a heroic figure when in a blood-soaked shirt. Not many people in the game have experienced as much as Butcher. So, if you have a question, drop it in the form below and we will put it to him. Continue reading...

general.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
general.summary: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments.
